follow-on: 'assert elapsed < WORKER_SLEEP_SECONDS' can never fail. The preceding _wait_until returns only when the supervisor's pid is gone within CEILING_SECONDS (90 s), and WORKER_SLEEP_SECONDS is 120 s, so elapsed < 90 < 120 always; when the escalation is withheld the wait itself raises first. The line reads as a second upper-bound guard but adds none -- the discriminator is the 90 s ceiling sitting under the worker's own sleep. Same shape at line 299. Not harmful; noted so a later reader does not rely on it as a bound. If a separate wall-clock assertion is wanted it must sit under the ceiling, or be derived from the poll the supervisor actually paid.

follow-on: no test drives the production stop grace. Both cases set RECKON_WORKER_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS=1 through the env, so STOP_GRACE_DEFAULT (10 s, line 8447) and the empty/ValueError/negative-falls-through branches of _stop_grace_seconds() are unexercised -- a defect that returned a nonsensical value when the env is unset would not be caught. The prior review noted the same gap and the repair did not close it. Fix direction: one case with the env unset asserting the default is read, or a direct unit call over the three branches.

It is attributable: the SIGKILL path calls routing.signal_worker with reason 'worker-ignored-the-stop-grace-signal' into the run's sender record, which the test asserts. The covering test fails when the escalation is withheld -- reproduced by me (negative control EXIT=1 on the bound case). Weaker points, neither fixed by the repair and both noted as findings: (a) neither case drives the production default stop grace -- both set RECKON_WORKER_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS=1 via the env -- so STOP_GRACE_DEFAULT (10 s) and the floor/ValueError branches of _stop_grace_seconds() are unexercised; (b) the elapsed < WORKER_SLEEP_SECONDS assertions are unreachable-as-failures once the 90 s bounded wait returns.

justifications.fit: The change sits where the grace machinery already lives: STOP_GRACE_ENV/STOP_GRACE_DEFAULT sit beside _WORKER_GRACE_KILL_SECONDS, and _stop_grace_seconds() is a sibling of _terminal_manifest_grace_seconds(), reading the same '+ env override, floor at zero' idiom. The two new keyword parameters thread onto the single existing caller and default to None/0.0 so no other call site changes. Names read as what the code does (stop_grace_seconds, worker-ignored-the-stop-grace-signal, run-stop); no version suffixes, no plan/sprint/ticket identifiers in symbols or comments, no AI attribution. The test module docstring states the mechanism rather than a ticket id.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The done-when is met and I reproduced it. The recorded defect was a supervisor that survives a crew stop: its SIGTERM handler only records the stop, then the reap loop blocks in os.waitpid for as long as the worker lives, so a worker that ignores the group stop holds the supervisor (and its slot) unbounded. The fix bounds that wait in the reap loop itself: _reap_worker_on_its_terminal_manifest (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:8562+) now takes stop_requested and stop_grace_seconds, and once the stop Event is set it re-signals the worker with SIGTERM reason 'run-stop' and then SIGKILLs it with reason 'worker-ignored-the-stop-grace-signal' after the grace (dispatch.py:8610-8637). The stop Event is the supervisor's own handler event (_record_stop_before_spawn, dispatch.py:8311), which fires because crew stop -> terminate() signals the worker's whole process group. The bound is the existing 3 s reap poll plus the configured stop grace plus the exit-record write; STOP_GRACE_DEFAULT reuses the pre-existing 10 s _WORKER_*_KILL_SECONDS and is overridable via RECKON_WORKER_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS. The test asserts the supervisor's pid is gone within a bounded wait and that the run's own sender record names the kill. I re-ran the gate at head (2 passed, EXIT=0) and the declared mutation (the bound case fails, EXIT=1).

No plan HTML, ledger, index or sprint state is touched. As at the prior head, the node also declared an evidence fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/a-crew-process-ends-with-its-owner/ and a docs/figures directory and emitted neither; that is an under-delivery, not a scope breach, and the done-when names only the test artifact.
